soundness_flags.label: def:oracle-recursion / thm:joint-expansion
soundness_flags.one_line: The graph permits donor-indexed coefficients c_{rju}, but beta_r is declared unit-invariant, so the asserted factor recursion does not close unless c_{rju}=c_{ru} or node coefficients are made donor-specific.

soundness_flags.label: target_estimand / def:path-value
soundness_flags.one_line: No potential-outcome or LTV-blip relation identifies each mu_{i0,r}, and hence V^pi, with a counterfactual path value rather than an arbitrary linear functional of observed-coordinate means.

soundness_flags.label: thm:joint-expansion, thm:gaussian-approximation, thm:replay-covariance
soundness_flags.one_line: The class gives only pointwise convergence p_N/N^{2+delta}->infinity and Sigma_N->Sigma, with no uniform rate or class-wide lower bound on delta, so the repeated claim 'uniformly over P' is not defined by the stated class.

soundness_flags.label: ass:outcome-factor
soundness_flags.one_line: The cited Synthetic-Blips LTV assumption is a potential-outcome, action-history, time-indexed additive factor model, not the stated static observed-coordinate equation Y_ih=v_i^T theta_h+eps_ih labeled as an LTV one-lag blip model.

soundness_flags.label: ass:feature-growth together with ass:covariate-independence
soundness_flags.one_line: The instrumental p_N>>N^{2+delta} regime requires more than quadratically many mutually independent proxy rows; the examples supplied do not establish that this measurement design is realistic or available in the intended panel application.

soundness_flags.label: ass:donor-gram
soundness_flags.one_line: Its upper spectral bound follows from ass:loading-bound, since the normalized donor Gram has operator norm at most max_i||v_i||_2^2.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The LTV model is specified for potential outcomes Y_n,t^(d̄_t) through time- and lag-indexed psi_n,t,l and action-history factors w_d_l, with conditional mean-zero potential-outcome innovations.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 21–22, Theorem 3 and discussion immediately following it
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 3 gives pointwise SBE-PCR consistency, and the paper explicitly describes it as point-wise consistency for fixed k and T.
The paper derives a scalar normal limit scaled by the growing number T1 of post-treatment periods, conditional on projected-weight conditions.
The paper treats standard static synthetic control and separates uncertainty from pre-treatment weight estimation and post-treatment prediction error.

source_verification_receipts.version: Quarterly Journal of Economics 139(1), 2024, version of record
source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract and Section III, 'Setting and Inference Problem'
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The target is inference on the true effect of the option selected by a given winner rule, addressing winner's-curse bias.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the abstract graph with a genuine LTV potential-outcome/blip model, state the path-to-node mapping, and either make c_{rju} donor-invariant or define a coherent donor-specific recursion before retaining any causal or influence claim.

Define a uniform triangular-array subclass with fixed constants, a common delta lower bound, and explicit rates for proxy growth and covariance convergence; state every uniform theorem over that subclass only.

Treat p_N/N^{2+delta} as an explicitly narrow sufficient regime, add a practically credible proxy-row dependence model, and make the frontier OEQ target weaker p-growth or dependence conditions rather than relying on mutually independent high-frequency rows.

recommended_next_step: Revise the causal model, recursion, and uniformity/practicality conditions, then return this angle for a fresh novelty review before Stage 0.
